messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find libraries in three cities with specific facilities. We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each city with appropriate facilities. The function signature: location: string, facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

We need to pass an array of facilities? The type says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; That seems ambiguous: maybe facilities can be a single string or an array of strings? The example says "Cafe"[] meaning array of "Cafe"? Actually "Cafe"[] means array of "Cafe" type? But "Cafe" is a string literal type. So maybe facilities can be an array of strings from that set. So we should pass an array of strings: e.g., ["Reading Room", "Fiction"].

Thus we need to call the function three times:

1. location: "New York, NY", facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]
2. location: "Los Angeles, CA", facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]
3. location: "Chicago, IL", facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"]

We need to call the function for each. The function returns any. We need to output the results. We'll call the function three times.
